h: "Their Ornaments from Mount Chorev": Gifts Taken from Esav and Yishmael

p: בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קצג, א):
"Come and see: the ornaments of the Children of Yisrael —
these are the gifts and presents
for they received presents and gifts from all of them.
Once they sinned, what is written?
וַיִּתְנַצְּלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת עֶדְיָם (שְׁמוֹת לג, ו);
'And the Children of Yisrael stripped themselves of their ornaments' (Shemos 33:6);
these are the 'gifts among men,' etc."
Earlier the Zohar said at length
that Esav and his angelic prince, Samech-Mem,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְזָרַח מִשֵּׂעִיר (דְּבָרִים לג, ב);
as it says, "And He shone forth from Se'ir" (Devarim 33:2):
And likewise from the prince of Yishmael:
and it explains that about this it says,
with which Yisrael were crowned at Matan Torah,
and one corresponding to "we will hear."
דְּאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה טז, י, פָּרָשַׁת שְׁלַח):
for it says in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah 16:10, Parshas Shelach):
Esav — 'he does the will of his Maker';
For the completion of the holiness
was in the middah of fear,
as it says at the last test:
כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית כב, יב);
that you are one who fears G-d" (Bereishis 22:12);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קלג, ב):
and as it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 133b):
"that fire was included together with water —
Therefore, on account of his completion
he called the son who came out of him
who knew that the completion of his holiness
would be perfected in the middah
as it says (in the Zohar I, there) —
"he does the will of his Maker,"
for they brought their powers into evil:
his power of might only for murder,
to murder and to conquer the world.
only for bodily cravings and evil desires;
each in the middah of the other.
And this is what it says:
what they took from Esav, the power of "we will do";
for "there is wisdom in Edom — believe it,"
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם (עוֹבַדְיָה א, ח)
as it says, "And I will destroy the wise men from Edom" (Ovadyah 1:8)
that is, the wisdom of Torah she'b'al peh,
only to conquer the yetzer hara.
the power of love and the power of "we will hear."
And had Yisrael been made complete
then the pasuk would have been fulfilled:
"And the nations shall be utterly destroyed" (Yeshayah 60:12);
and from Mount Chorev there would have been destruction
for the nations of the world.
And this is "their ornaments from Mount Chorev."
And then there would have been the completion of the tikkun,
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם (תְּהִלִּים פב, ו),
that they would not have died
וְהָיָה נִתְבַּטֵּל הַמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
and the Angel of Death and the yetzer hara would have been nullified,
And afterward, when they became corrupted,
it is written: "And the Children of Yisrael stripped themselves
of their ornaments from Mount Chorev" —
corresponding to "we will do" and "we will hear,"
on account of which it is called Chorev,
And there remained only what they took captive as spoils,
as it says in the holy Zohar there —
until they bring out all the vitality
from the nations of the world in exile;
for this was the purpose of the exiles:
that converts be added to them
all the power of the yetzer hara,
which is the kelipah of Amalek, the evil inclination
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קס, א).
(as it says in the Zohar III 160a).
only they changed their language to the language of Canaan
כְּתִיב אֶצְלָם: וַיִּשְׁבְּ מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁבִי (בַּמִּדְבָּר כא, א),
it is written of them, "and he took of him captives" (Bamidbar 21:1),
that he took back even the captives,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
as it says in the holy Zohar cited above.

inlineHeadings.text: The ornaments of Yisrael: gifts from the princes of the nations
The Gemara: two crowns for each Jew
Fair names and ugly deeds: Yishmael and Esav
Had they not sinned: destruction from Chorev
The exiles: bringing out the holy sparks

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 193a (Balak) — "Come and see: the ornaments of the Children of Israel are the gifts and presents they received, and therefore neither death nor the Other Side ruled over them. Not only did they take the Torah without any challenge — they received presents and gifts from all of them. Once they sinned, what is written? 'And the Children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments' (Shemos 33:6)."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 1 — “We also find, ‘the kindness of the nations,’ that there is in them the attribute of Chesed, and this is from Yishmael, the dross of Avraham's Chesed… and the wisdom of Esav is from the dross of Yitzchak's Gevurah… And I have already spoken on what is written, ‘He shone forth from Seir and appeared from Mount Paran.’” Connection: Both read Devarim 33:2 as Torah's light drawn out of Seir and Paran, the husks of Esav and Yishmael.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 88a — “Rabbi Simai expounded: When Israel placed 'We will do' before 'We will hear,' six hundred thousand ministering angels came, and tied two crowns to each individual of Israel, one corresponding to 'We will do' and one to 'We will hear.' When Israel sinned, twelve hundred thousand destructive angels descended and removed them, as it says: 'The children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Chorev.' Rabbi Yochanan said: Moshe merited them all and took them. Reish Lakish said: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will return them to us, as it says: 'Those redeemed by Hashem will return and come to Zion with song, with everlasting joy upon their heads'—the joy that had been upon their heads from of old. Rabbi Elazar said: When Israel placed 'We will do' before 'We will hear,' a heavenly voice went forth: 'Who revealed to My children this secret used by the ministering angels?' For it is written: 'Bless Hashem, His angels, mighty in strength, who perform His word, to hear the voice of His word'—first performing, and afterward hearing.” This is the source both for the two crowns and for the angelic precedence of doing over hearing. Its account of Moshe receiving the lost crowns and their eventual restoration also underlies the ensuing discussion.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 133b (Chayei Sarah) — "'And Avraham gave all that he had to Yitzchak' (Bereishis 25:5)… Here water was included in fire, and fire in water. At first fire was included in water — when? At the time he bound Yitzchak to execute judgment upon him; and now water was included in fire, so that all be the secret of supernal faith."

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 5a — "As this Tanna taught: Rabbi Yosi says: Israel accepted the Torah only so that the Angel of Death would not rule over them, as it says, 'I said: you are angels, all of you children of the Most High' — you corrupted your deeds — 'therefore like men you shall die' (Tehillim 82:6–7)."

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 16a — "Reish Lakish said: He is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the Angel of Death. He is the Satan, as it is written, 'And the Satan went out from before Hashem' (Iyov 2:7); he is the evil inclination, as it is written there, 'only evil all day' (Bereishis 6:5)…; he is the Angel of Death, as it is written, 'only guard his soul' (Iyov 2:6)."

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 87b — “Rabbi Elazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, exiled Israel among the nations only so that converts might be added to them, as it says, ‘I shall sow her for Myself in the land.’ Does a person sow a se’ah except to bring in many kor?” The Gemara expressly speaks of converts and compares exile with sowing. The extension to holy sparks within the nations belongs to the mystical explanation cited by Rav Tzadok.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 160a, Shelach — “Furthermore, ‘Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev.’ If a person says that despite all this he will attain it: ‘Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev’—this is the evil inclination, the accuser, who accuses a person and is constantly found in the body. ‘The Hittite and the Amorite’—how many accusers are found there, so that a person cannot enter that world at all. Who will merit it, and who will enter it? With these words ‘they disheartened the children of Israel,’ for they brought out an evil report about it.” The Zohar first portrays the discouraging accusation, then answers it with sincere will and guarding the covenant. This exact context supports Rav Tzadok's identification of Amalek as the accusing root of the inclination.

p: to bring out the holy sparks.
to make for it a dwelling
in the two chambers of the heart,
and the yetzer hara is cleared out from there
(as it says in Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48) —
that is, to empty the heart of all evil,
which is the kelipah of Amalek, the evil inclination —
"And the nations shall be utterly destroyed" (Yeshayah 60:12) —
from Mount Chorev they shall be destroyed.
And this is what the Arizal wrote:
that they merited at Matan Torah,
corresponding to "we will do" and "we will hear,"
and which Moshe merited and took
in the gift of his portion" —
that he merited at Matan Torah
and then he returns the crowns to Yisrael,
and "the nations shall be utterly destroyed,"

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48, 85a — "Fortunate is he who makes them a dwelling on Shabbos in the two chambers of the heart, so that the evil inclination, which is the desecration of Shabbos, is cleared out from there."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta, Ohev Yisrael, Vayakhel — “[At Sinai each one of Israel received] two crowns; afterward, when they sinned with the Calf, this departed from them, as it says, ‘And the Children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Chorev’ (Shemos 33:6): all the illumination of holiness they had received at Chorev was lost. All the lights and crowns, the ornaments of Israel taken from them at Chorev, Moshe Rabbeinu took for himself. But Moshe is a faithful servant, and on holy Shabbos, when holiness rests upon Israel, he returns the crowns to each one of Israel, and each receives according to his holiness, as is known from the Arizal's kavanah on ‘Moshe rejoiced in the gift of his portion.’” Connection: The ornaments stripped at Chorev, which Rav Tzadok explains from the Zohar, are here shown returning each Shabbos through Moshe.
